searchText: <@393119312350543872> we talked in EOF call to merge EOF verification related test (this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/tests/pull/1339), those does not have fillers but are very useful for testing. It would be easier to iterate for us when they are merged. If it doesn't have fillers I can't track its updates and can't ask other eof tools to regenerate or track how they execute it. Does eof planned to be included into next HF? Yeah, EOF is very probably going in Prague. We could have at least two evm impls check (manually) if new changes are okay, but we need a place where those changes are going to converge. Idea is to find the way in future to convert those to standard test, but in meantime merging them in this form would be helpful. Do you want python scripts support for this type of tests? So that you can use scripting to design the bytecode ? It is better question for <@907931206081990666>, <@275684146658148352>, would assume these are low priority rn and endgoal would be to use statetest for it (It seems possible to trigger them with TXCREATE) Thats how I initially was doing that. But we went with t9n tool that covers some few cases that TXCREATE can't. If you can use state test format for it, you can use python scripts already. What is your current approach to generate eof code? `evmone` has a basic DSL which supports formatting of (some) opcodes and outputs formatted eof containers, random example from `evmone`'s tests to give an idea: ``` deploy_container = eof_bytecode(bytecode(OP_DATALOADN) + "0040" + ret_top(), 2).data(deploy_data, deploy_data_size); init_container = eof_bytecode(returncontract(0, 0, 32), 2).container(deploy_container); eof_bytecode(sstore(0, eofcreate().container(0).input(0, 0).salt(Salt)) + sstore(1, 1) + OP_STOP, 4).container(init_container); ``` I think we can make it much user friendlier in python scripts. And most importantly the scripts will hold the source and the logic, not a bytecode so the tests will be editable
